title: Radius-Guided Post-Clustering for Shape-Aware, Scalable Refinement of k-Means Results
summary: The paper addresses k-means' need to specify k in advance and its poor recovery of non-convex clusters by adding a geometric post-processing step. After standard k-means with an intentionally high k, it assigns each center a radius to its farthest assigned point and merges clusters whose center distance is within the sum of radii, using connected components; it also sketches tiled recursive partitioning. On FCPS benchmarks, radius-guided merging reports median clustering success of 98–100% across overestimated k values, including 1.0 on FCPS Atom with k=20.

match_target.why: Cheapest claim that still shows the paper's central post-processing result: a small FCPS Atom 2-D run with k=20 directly matches the user's target and demonstrates radius-based recovery after over-segmentation.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: clustering success is a bounded score printed in [0,1] on FCPS Atom (<2,000 points), and the paper reports only IQR 0.0 rather than std, so use 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Run standard k-means on FCPS Atom with intentionally overestimated k=20 before post-processing.
requirements.quote: After running standard k-means (with an intentionally large k)

requirements.stmt: Compute each cluster radius as the maximum Euclidean distance from its centroid to any assigned point.
requirements.quote: we compute a radius for each cluster Ci as the maximum distance from its centroid ci to any of its assigned points:

requirements.stmt: Merge clusters when the center distance is at most the sum of their radii.
requirements.quote: two clusters are merged if their radius-based boundaries would overlap

requirements.stmt: Implement merging through a connectivity graph and connected components rather than iterative pairwise merging.
requirements.quote: Clusters belonging to the same connected component in this graph are merged

requirements.stmt: Propagate merged-component labels back to every point in the component.
requirements.quote: Clusters belonging to the same connected component in this graph are merged, and the new labels are propagated accordingly.

requirements.stmt: Use only standard k-means outputs, namely cluster centers and point assignments, for post-processing.
requirements.quote: relies only on standard outputs of k-means: cluster centers and point assignments

requirements.stmt: Repeat each experiment 100 times and keep the best of five runs as stated for the reported medians.
requirements.quote: Each experiment was repeated 100 times, and the best of five runs was kept.

requirements.stmt: Report median clustering success and interquartile range across runs.
requirements.quote: reporting median clustering success and interquartile range across runs

requirements.stmt: Evaluate against ground-truth labels using clustering success/overlap, not only the unsupervised k-means objective.
requirements.quote: Values represent the median clustering success in recovering ground-truth labels

requirements.stmt: Exclude FCPS Engytime from the full FCPS-suite evaluation.
requirements.quote: One dataset, FCPS Engytime, was excluded from evaluation

requirements.stmt: Build the method atop scikit-learn's k-means implementation.
requirements.quote: Implemented as a lightweight post-processing step atop scikit-learn’s k-means

requirements.stmt: For the tiled extension, split the feature space into four quadrants and use local k as a percentage of each tile's points before global radius merging.
requirements.quote: Each dataset was split into four quadrants by partitioning the feature space in half along the first two dimensions.
